scope: 18 A1 speaking and writing items from batches 073 and 074; source text and authored scene/alt consistency.
method: Read the complete sources and starters. Reconstruct person, intention, medium, recipient and purpose from each prompt and scene before judging criteria, samples, models and scaffolds. Do not use earlier editorial passes, numerical ratings or author assurances as evidence. Allow the explicitly requested visual oddity; test whether the surrounding communication makes sense.

semantic_coherence_scale.2: Major role or medium conflict; the current prompt/scene does not support its act.
semantic_coherence_scale.3: Meaning is recoverable only by adding a material missing context.
semantic_coherence_scale.4: Coherent purpose with a small contextual looseness.
semantic_coherence_scale.5: Self-contained coherent task; the visual oddity does not obstruct meaning.

notes: All nine speaking descriptions are semantically coherent at authored-source level; one needs a starter correction.
Six speaking titles and three writing titles disclose picture-derived answers. Two writing items also have context defects; the remaining title cases are scaffold-only revisions.
Four writing tasks impose an underexplained written medium or recipient role on what their scene presents as an immediate exchange.
Five other writing tasks have coherent acts: invitation, event details, RSVP, sharing odd packaging, and replying to a received playful photo.
No item needs wholesale replacement on this source-text audit. Revise means the current item fails a concrete check while its central content goals remain locally repairable.

cross_item_findings.explanation: The prompt names a recipient and a message but does not establish why writing is the practical act in the authored scene. A correct-looking model and aligned criteria cannot supply that missing context.
A starter for one goal names the answer to another goal even though it remains syntactically incomplete.

The title is displayed in the exercise header. Six speaking titles and three writing titles disclose a fact asked for from the picture. The giant-cup and kitchen-dance titles supply both speaking goals; other flagged titles supply one goal. Theme words and facts already supplied in the prompt are not treated as new answer leakage.

implementation_evidence.meaning: The exercise header displays the authored title to the learner.

limitations: No media was generated or fetched, and no provider or browser was called. The report audits authored image briefs and alt text, not the rendered images or audio.
An editorial judgment about coherent beginner practice does not validate CEFR difficulty, learning outcomes or exam equivalence.
This audit records findings only. It changes no source exercises, starters, catalogue, production state or prior review artifact.

items.image_alt_audit: The onion and apples match the task, but the counter setting supplies the wrong medium for the prescribed communicative act.

findings.quote: U wilt een appel kopen. Kijk naar het plaatje. Schrijf een bericht aan de winkel. Zeg welk eten u krijgt. Vraag om een appel.
findings.related_quote: At a small fruit shop counter, a surprised adult customer holds open a paper shopping bag.
findings.explanation: The learner is staged at a seller’s counter but asked to write a shop message. No remote order, later discovery or written contact is given. The onion/apple mix-up can remain playful, but the present context does not make the prescribed message practical.

findings.related_quote: Ik krijg een ui. Mag ik een appel?
findings.explanation: Welk eten is an awkward way to refer to a single piece of produce here. The model reads as a spoken counter request and carries the same unresolved transaction context.

findings.related_quote: U wilt een appel kopen. Kijk naar het plaatje. Schrijf een bericht aan de winkel. Zeg welk eten u krijgt. Vraag om een appel.

prompt_scene_reconstruction.recipient: Roos, the breakfast preparer shown presenting the cake at the table.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.why: A guest could naturally comment on a cake and name a drink to a host. The supplied scene supports saying that to Roos. It gives no photo, advance breakfast planning or other reason to message her while she presents the cake.

source_evidence.model: Ik vind de taart mooi. Ik wil graag thee drinken.

items.criteria_audit: The criteria exactly match giving an opinion and naming a wanted drink. An opinion about appearance, such as mooi, is valid; the learner need not taste the cake.

sample_quotes_audit.reason: The sample omits the indicated content goal and still conveys the other. Its deliberate beginner errors remain understandable; the quoted support is verbatim.

items.model_audit: The model gives an opinion and a preferred drink in natural simple Dutch. Its adequacy at sentence level does not establish why this should be a message.

starter_audit.reason: The opinion and drink fragments align and leave the opinion and drink choice open.

items.image_alt_audit: The cake agrees with the prompt. Roos serving it in person leaves the written medium unsupported.

findings.quote: Roos maakt ontbijt voor u. Er staat een taart op tafel. Schrijf een bericht aan Roos.
findings.related_quote: Roos (young woman, dark hair in a bun, yellow scarf) proudly presents an unexpectedly tall cake at a small breakfast table.
findings.explanation: The communicative goals suit a breakfast conversation, while the source specifically puts the addressee at the table presenting the cake. A message can work in a different temporal or remote context, but that context is not supplied. The tall cake itself is a coherent visual joke.

items.reason: The socked chair is intelligible, but the message to a teacher about whether that pictured classroom seat is free lacks a reservation or remote-planning context.

prompt_scene_reconstruction.person: The learner is a student who wants to use one distinctive classroom chair.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.intention: Identify the preferred chair and check whether it is available.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.medium: A written message is prescribed; the given context chiefly supports an immediate seat question.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.recipient: The teacher, with no assigned-seat or reservation role established.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.why: A student can ask about a seat. The source does not say the class uses assigned seats or bookings, or why the student messages the teacher about a visibly unoccupied chair. A remote reservation interpretation requires extra context.
prompt_scene_reconstruction.scene: An unoccupied chair with socks on its legs stands beside a desk; another empty chair is farther away.

title_audit.reason: The title gives a scene theme or repeats context already stated in the prompt; it does not supply a new exact answer to a production goal.

items.criteria_audit: The criteria match identifying the socked chair and asking if it is free. Vrij can mean unoccupied or available, so the picture alone does not prove the answer; the problem is why this is a message to the teacher.

sample_quotes_audit.reason: The sample omits the indicated content goal and still conveys the other. Its deliberate beginner errors remain understandable; the quoted support is verbatim.

items.model_audit: The model expresses desire for the chair and asks about availability. It is understandable but gives the message no practical purpose beyond the imposed exercise.

starter_audit.reason: The preferred-chair and availability fragments fit the goals and do not supply sokken or vrij.

items.image_alt_audit: The socks are coherent chair-leg covers and can stay. The empty-chair scene supplies no reason for a teacher-managed written request.

findings.quote: In uw klas staat een stoel met sokken. U wilt daar zitten. Schrijf een bericht aan de docent.
findings.related_quote: Ik wil de stoel met sokken. Is deze stoel nog vrij?
findings.explanation: The task asks for a teacher-directed message about an available classroom chair without a seating-plan, reservation, photo or advance-planning context. The learner must invent a reason to write. The chair’s socks are a readable visual oddity and are not the defect.
